_doc: Subset-decision register (roadmap P-SURF S7.2). Each entry attributes test262 core-incompatible cases to a recorded decision instead of an implementation. cluster_incompat.py applies each entry's predicate mechanically and reports attributed mass beside the gate numbers. Sign-off is delegated per takagi 2026-08-11 (decide-by-principles); entries remain takagi-vetoable.

entries.title: sloppy-only surface (noStrict-flagged cases)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: tr's language surface is TypeScript modules; module code is always strict (ES §16.2). The reference baseline bun runs .ts as ESM — the same always-strict surface. A noStrict-flagged case requires sloppy semantics for its assertions to hold and is not expressible as a TS module on either runtime: a language-definition boundary, not a missing feature. A sloppy/script mode would be a product-surface expansion foreign to TS; if ever authorized it becomes a post-v1.0 roadmap phase and this entry retires. Does NOT cover strict-semantics gaps where tr still leaks sloppy behaviour (e.g. the B.3.3 block-fn leak) — those stay implementation debt.

entries.title: source-phase imports proposal (ModuleSource / import source)
entries.signoff: agent, per takagi delegation 2026-08-11; takagi retains veto
entries.rationale: source-phase-imports is a stage-3 proposal (import source / %AbstractModuleSource%), not a ratified ECMA-262 clause. The reference baseline bun (stable 1.3.14) rejects the `import source` syntax at parse, so no oracle exists on the baseline either; per the test262 discipline this entry records WHY rather than skipping silently: the phase semantics presuppose a module-source reification layer that tr's AOT compile-and-link model has no design for yet — a post-v1.0 roadmap phase, not an out-of-scope decision. The entry retires (cases return to the substrate queue) when the proposal is ratified or bun ships it, whichever is first.
